rationale: The aim is to improve a local care process quickly, with changes adapted between cycles, which is what the Model for Improvement is for. Case-by-case run charts fit seven or eight cases a month (c5). The evidence supports the change ideas (c1, c2) and names the balancing measures (c4). Reporting follows SQUIRE 2.0.
alternatives: Before-and-after comparison of two annual medians (refused: too slow and confounded)
Stepped introduction across network hospitals (refused: one hospital, local aim)
whyNotMoreComplex: A controlled comparison would need several hospitals and a stable intervention; the team needs to adapt changes case by case.

decision.statement: Map the thrombolysis pathway with all involved staff and test changes in PDSA cycles from January to June 2027, starting with direct-to-CT transfer and a single group page (c1, c2), plotting every case on a run chart (c5) and reviewing haemorrhage and treated mimics as balancing measures (c4).
decision.question: Should the stroke centre run a mapping and PDSA project on door-to-needle time, and which changes first?

criteria.text: The targeted steps are where most delay occurs, and a comparable centre shortened them.

gates.requirement: Emergency department and stroke program approval of the project
gates.evidence: Approval memo SP-2026-14 dated 2026-08-21, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Ethics office determination that the project is quality improvement
gates.evidence: Screening QI-SCR-26-203 dated 2026-09-02, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Monthly feedback of door-to-needle medians without pathway changes
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2, c4 and c5 from retrieved records; the leads are not cited. Both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.

summary: QI with mapping and PDSA cycles recommended; both gates met.
